Who this is for

For people who've tried
tracking — and stopped.

You already know what you want to change. The hard part isn't motivation — it's friction. It's the app that turns into a chore. The streak that makes you feel worse when you break it. The data that tells you what happened but never why.

Forged is for people who think in patterns. Who want to actually understand their behaviour, not just record it. Who'd rather spend 30 seconds logging something real than 10 minutes fighting an interface.

Other apps track what happened. Forged helps you understand why — and what to do next.

Your AI habit coach

Ask it anything.
It knows your habits.

The Forged AI coach isn't a chatbot bolted on. It knows what you've logged, what you've written, how long your streaks are, and where things fell apart last time. Real answers, not generic advice.

🎙️
Voice and quick-prompt logging Don't want to type? Say it. Forged captures it and attaches it to the right habit — no friction, no tapping through menus.
🔍
Pattern detection from your own data Why do you skip Thursdays? What changed when your streak hit 14 days? The coach finds it.
💬
Chat about your progress in plain language Ask it what to focus on next week. Ask it why something isn't working. It knows your context.
⚡
Available everywhere in the app On your Today screen, your Insights page, your Journal — the coach is always one tap away.

How it works

Up and running
in sixty seconds.

01

Set up what you're working on

Pick your habits and goals. Forged creates your first set based on what matters to you — and you can edit everything.

02

Log daily in seconds

One tap for simple habits. A voice note or quick prompt when something's worth capturing. Less friction than anything else.

03

Talk to your coach

Ask the AI anything. It knows what you've logged, what you've written, how long your streaks are, and where things fell apart. Real answers, not generic tips.

04

Bring someone in

Add an accountability partner. Share a goal. Start showing up for each other — and knowing when they haven't.
